documents.title: Stop data centers in Johnson County, Texas (petition, undated; read 2026-10-30)
documents.text: A resident petition asks Johnson County commissioners for a more measured approach to data-center growth, noting a data center can be built with only a basic development permit. No county moratorium has been proposed. Petition text: "The only way the commissioners may even know that a data center is pursuing our county is if they come requesting tax incentives." Petition text: "So far, Johnson County has rejected 2 requests for such tax abatements for data centers."

events.title: Governor directs PUCT and ERCOT to audit data centers in the interconnection queue; ERCOT pauses Batch Zero
PUCT grants ERCOT good-cause exceptions for the audit timeline
Governor directs TCEQ to "halt all permits sought by data centers until the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) completes its audit"

approval.value: No zoning approval: Johnson County has no zoning authority outside cities. Expect county platting, floodplain review and site permits.
approval.note: Texas counties have no general zoning authority (Tex. Loc. Gov. Code ch. 231), per Atria zoning jurisdiction. Hill County adopted a data-center moratorium in 2026 and rescinded it after a federal lawsuit argued Texas counties lack that authority.
approval.source: Atria: zoning jurisdiction + Texas Local Government Code
